subject: Streaming perf qualification & reproducibility playbook (Novaretail)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@novaretail.com>, Devon Price <devon.price@novaretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: streaming perf targets & next steps

Hi Maya / Devon,

Thanks again for the demo today — good conversation. As promised, I wanted to capture our understanding of the SLO/qualification needs for the streaming use case and clarify the immediate asks so we can scope a reproducible benchmark run. Please confirm or correct anything below.

Redwood's read of your requirements (call highlights):
- Workload: customer-facing chat with streaming token-by-token output (frontend expects early token emission).
- Target latency: p95 end-to-end token-chunk delivery ~200ms (network + infer chunk).
- Throughput: sustained ~80 requests/sec across the fleet during peak (burst to 120 rps tolerated).
- Concurrency: expected active concurrency 40-60 simultaneous sessions; spikes to ~100 for short windows.
- Output shape: variable length responses (median ~120 tokens, long-tail to 800 tokens); streaming should avoid large initial buffering.
- Quality: top-k generation acceptable if within your post-filtering rules — you'll share prompt-level pass/fail examples.

Immediate asks from Novaretail for the first reproducibility run:
1) Sample prompt set (representative user messages + expected pass/fail tags) — you mentioned sending CSV export.
2) Confirmation of the exact p95 target (200ms is our note) and whether you want p50/p95/p99 reported for both first-byte and whole-response completion.
3) A short trace or description of client-side streaming expectations (chunk size, throttling) so we can mirror JS event timing.
4) Any compliance constraints (no telemetry beyond token-level metrics) or IP restrictions for artifacts.

What we'll deliver in the first reproducible run (proposed):
- A portable harness run (Docker + manifest) that replays your prompt set with streaming enabled and outputs token-timing traces, per-request metrics (latency percentiles, tokens/sec), and an artifact containing the raw model outputs for QA.
- A sizing & model-variant recommendation based on observed throughput with our initial run.
- A short mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and owners.

Proposed timeline:
- You send sample prompt set + answers to the questions above by end of day 2026-11-17.
- Redwood runs an initial reproducible harness by 2026-11-20 and shares artifacts + a short write-up.

Attachments: I'll add a lightweight checklist (internal) and our preferred manifest template after your sample arrives.

Next steps: Please confirm the CSV(s) are on the way and whether any of the targets above need adjustment. If it helps, we're available for a 30-minute follow-up tomorrow to walk through the manifest and streaming knobs.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-17T09:30:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: streaming perf targets & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming items and attaching a representative prompt sample. A few clarifications inline.

Attachments: novaretail_prompt_samples.csv (600 rows; columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_behavior)

Clarifications:
- Latency target: yes, 200ms p95 for streaming token-chunk delivery is the target. We also want p50/p95 for both first-token and final-token completion. p99 useful but not blocking for phase 1.
- Throughput/concurrency: sustained 80 rps is correct; expected concurrency 50 typical, but infrastructure should tolerate spikes to 110 for ~2 minute windows.
- Streaming semantics: client receives tokens as they arrive; frontend commits UI after receiving first 6 tokens. Chunk size is effectively single-token emit from model runtime. Please mirror token timing, not buffered batches.
- Quality: we'll annotate ~50 prompts as PASS/FAIL for quick spot checks. Those are included in column expected_behavior.
- Data constraints: prompt samples are anonymized; for full runs we'll share a redacted set or host the dataset in a temporary cloud bucket with S3 pre-signed link.

Other asks for Redwood: can you include first-byte (server -> client) timing breakdown and an estimate of GPU-hours required for a 10k-query reproducible run? Also, if you propose a model variant (e.g., rwinf-7b-q4 or rwinf-13b-ggml), please include expected cost delta.

We're good for the timeline — we'll push the CSV to the link below by EOD 11/17.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Gupta
Director, Platform Engineering — Novaretail
maya.gupta@novaretail.com

Related link: https://drive.google.com/novaretail/prompt-samples

Marissa / Rishi / Maya — thanks, forwarding a concise tech plan and the manifest we intend to run. I'm copying Maya so Novaretail can flag any divergence from their client semantics.

High-level plan (tech):
- Harness: we'll use the replay harness (containerized) that opens a streaming websocket per session and replays tokens according to the timestamps we record. For this run we will not inject client-side jitter; we'll mirror token emit timing.
- Measurement: report per-request metrics: first-token latency, final-token latency, token-emission inter-arrival stats, tokens/sec, and system metrics (GPU util, mem, PCIe). We'll compute p50/p95/p99 for first/final token.
- Reproducibility: the run will include a manifest (novaretail_harness_manifest.yaml) that fixes model version, RNG seed, batch config, sequence length caps, and measurement window. We'll publish the manifest + run script in the Drive link.
- Models & sizing (initial estimate):
  - rwinf-7b-q4: expected p95 first-token ~140-220ms at 50 concurrency; approximate GPU-hours for 10k queries: 1.5 GPU-hours on an A10G-equivalent with continuous seating (cost estimate: $X).
  - rwinf-13b-ggml: expected p95 first-token ~220-380ms at 50 concurrency; approximate GPU-hours for 10k queries: 3.5 GPU-hours (cost estimate: $Y).
(We will provide a more rigorous estimate after the 1k sanity run).

Deliverables and timeline (confirming Marissa's plan):
- 11/18: run 1k warmup + 2k measurement (internal) and push artifacts to Drive.
- 11/20: full 10k reproducible run + results + sizing write-up.

Attachments: novaretail_harness_manifest.yaml (stub)
